Four platforms (Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge, Deno Deploy, Fly.io) dominate the category, each making a different trade-off between developer experience, cost, and what your code is allowed to do. The marketing is mostly indistinguishable. The real-world fit is not.

What I'll cover: the actual differences between the four, the pricing math that becomes obvious only at production volume, the hidden constraint that broke that Twilio migration, and how to pick the platform that matches your actual workload.

## 3. Netlify

Netlify

Netlify is the platform that popularized JAMstack hosting and remains Vercel's closest head-to-head competitor. Both offer Git-push deployments, deploy previews, edge and serverless functions, and a $20/seat pro plan.

Netlify ships several features Vercel doesn't match natively: built-in forms handling (no backend needed to accept submissions), Netlify Identity for authentication, and split testing at the CDN level. ## Executive Summary

Edge computing has shifted from experimental to default deployment architecture in 2026, with edge functions delivering 9x faster cold starts and 2x execution speed compared to traditional serverless. Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge Functions, and Deno Deploy now power production applications across 300+ global data centers, processing 80% of AI inference locally rather than in cloud data centers. WebAssembly runtimes achieve sub-millisecond cold starts, while new pricing models (Cloudflare's $0.011 per 1,000 Neurons) make edge deployment economically compelling at scale.

### Cold Start Performance

Edge functions deliver dramatic improvements over traditional serverless:

 Cloudflare Workers: Sub-1ms cold starts via V8 isolates
 Edge Functions (general): 9x faster than traditional serverless (5ms vs 100ms-1000ms)
 WebAssembly Runtime: Under 1 millisecond cold start times
